name: Following
momentumNotes: Progress comes by following the living current rather than imposing a rigid plan.
theme: Following is not passive drifting. It is the art of responding to what is alive, true, and already in motion.
basicInterpretation: Loosen the need to lead every step. The right path may reveal itself through listening, companionship, and timely adjustment.
reflectionPrompt: What becomes possible if you follow what is sincerely moving?

reversed.theme: Flipped upside down, Following becomes Hexagram 18, Work on What Has Been Spoiled. This other side brings in the atmosphere of repair, neglect, inheritance, asking how the situation may look from another threshold.
reversed.reflection: Let Work on What Has Been Spoiled widen the reading rather than replace it. Consider what another person, timing, or hidden part of you might see when the pattern is viewed from the far side.
reversed.applicationPrompt: Visualize your question from the far side, as if another person or your future self is looking back through Work on What Has Been Spoiled. Notice where repair, neglect, inheritance and a correcting, restoring movement reveal needs, timing, or motives that the first view may miss.

opposite.theme: The contrast to Following is Hexagram 18, Work on What Has Been Spoiled. Where the primary pattern emphasizes adaptation, trust, response, this complementary field points toward repair, neglect, inheritance.
opposite.reflection: In this reading, the complementary view is the same hexagram as the Other Side. This suggests that what the situation is not, and how it may appear from another angle, are part of the same teaching.
opposite.applicationPrompt: Visualize Work on What Has Been Spoiled as the contrasting color laid beside Following. Ask what hidden cause, missing medicine, or opposing pressure is suggested by repair, neglect, inheritance, especially where the situation carries a corrective, challenging tone.
